entries.title: Psalms 68:1
segments: The remarkable character of this psalm is best explained upon the supposition that it was written to be sung when the ark was carried in solemn procession to Jerusalem, either upon the occasion of its removal from the house of Obed-edom to Zion,

, or, as some think, at a later period, when it was brought back at the head of David's victorious army, whom it had accompanied in one of his wars. The ark was the divinely appointed symbol of God's presence.  Its entrance into Jerusalem, in triumphal procession, naturally recalled to the psalmist's mind the time when God came down from heaven to deliver his covenant people,

, went before them by the way of Sinai and the Arabian wilderness to the promised land, overthrew their enemies, and put them in possession of it.  All this he celebrates in the loftiest strains of lyric poetry, with some marked allusions to the song of Deborah and Barak; and, at the close, anticipates the day when this mighty God shall receive the homage of all nations. 
 
The writers of the New Testament regard God's descent from heaven for the salvation of his ancient people, as a prophetic type of the higher salvation which Jesus Christ wrought for his people, when he was made flesh and dwelt among men.  See note to

. 
 
  Let God arise; these are the words employed by Moses when the ark set forward,

.  They contain both a prayer and a prediction. 
 
Though God delay for a season to appear to his people, in due time he will arise and have mercy upon them, and will confound and destroy those who rise up against them.

entries.title: Psalms 68:4
segments:
Upon the heavens; rather, through the deserts; in allusion to God's guidance of the covenant people through the wilderness of Arabia. 
 
  Jah; an abbreviation of the word Jehovah.

entries.title: Psalms 68:6
segments:
Setteth the solitary in families; provides a home for the desolate and outcast. 
 
  Dwell in a dry land; where they are destitute of the comforts which he gives those who love and obey him.

entries.title: Psalms 68:7
segments: Wentest forth before thy people; in bringing them out of Egypt.  In this and the following verse the sacred writer agrees very closely with the words of Deborah and Barak's song.
The deliverance of God's people and his mercies to them in times past, are foretastes and earnests of what he will do for them in time to come.

entries.title: Psalms 68:8
segments: Dropped; as in a storm of thunder and lightning.

entries.title: Psalms 68:9
segments: A plentiful rain; most probably an allusion to the manna and quails, which are elsewhere described under the figure of rain.
Thine inheritance; Israel, as the heritage of God.

entries.title: Psalms 68:10
segments: Therein; in the promised land, to which the Israelites were brought through God's sustaining power in the wilderness.

entries.title: Psalms 68:11
segments:
Gave the word; the word of victory, when Israel took possession of Canaan. 
 
  Those that published it; the female singers that celebrated it. The allusion is to the choral songs of the Israelitish women with which they celebrated the victories of God's people.

The words of truth and love which God gives to his people encourage them to go forward in duty, putting their trust in him and expecting that he will finally give them the victory over all their foes.

entries.title: Psalms 68:12
segments: Did flee; the enemies of Israel.

entries.title: Psalms 68:13
segments:
Lain among the pots; wrought in brick and mortar in Egypt.  but some render the words, "when ye lie down among your folds;" that is, rest in peace, after the conquest of the land. 
 
Whatever may have been their former character or employment, when made partakers of divine mercy and adorned with the graces of the Holy Spirit, saints become beautiful and lovely in the eyes of the Lord of hosts and of all good beings.

entries.title: Psalms 68:14
segments:
In it; in the promised land. 
 
  White as snow; according to some, the meaning is, that the fields were white with the bones of God's enemies.  But the more probable reference is to the splendor of God's presence.

entries.title: Psalms 68:15
segments: The hill of God-- hill of Bashan; or, as we may render, "A hill of God is the hill of Bashan; a hill of [lofty] peaks is the hill of Bashan."  A hill of God means a very great and majestic hill.  The meaning of the psalmist is, that though Bashan may excel Zion in outward height and splendor, God has honored the latter by making it his peculiar abode.

entries.title: Psalms 68:16
segments: Leap ye; or, look askance; from envy at the honor conferred on the hill of Zion.

entries.title: Psalms 68:17
segments: Twenty thousand; put for a vast multitude.  The reference is to the angelic hosts who were present at the giving of the law on Sinai.
God has multitudes which no man can number, who at his call are ready to engage in his cause and fight against his foes.

entries.title: Psalms 68:18
segments: Received gifts; applied by the apostle Paul to the ascension gifts bestowed by Christ upon his church.

entries.title: Psalms 68:20
segments: Issues; deliverance.

entries.title: Psalms 68:22
segments: I will bring again; according to some, I will bring my people home again from their dispersion.  But the connection favors the idea that the reference is rather to God's enemies, thus: Though they hide themselves from me in Bashan, or in the depths of the sea, thence will I bring them, that I may inflict upon them the punishment of their sins.  Compare
, where a similar figure is used.

entries.title: Psalms 68:23
segments:
Dipped in the blood of thine enemies; that they might utterly overcome them. 
 
Utter destruction is before the wicked; and except they repent, their ruin will be awful and sure.

entries.title: Psalms 68:24
segments:
They have seen; thy people. 
 
  Thy goings; in triumphal procession. 
 
  In the sanctuary; or, into the sanctuary on mount Zion.

entries.title: Psalms 68:26
segments: From the fountain of Israel; ye that come from the fountain of Israel, that is, the descendents of Israel.

entries.title: Psalms 68:27
segments:
Little Benjamin; the youngest of Jacob's sons, and also the smallest of the tribes present at the triumphal procession. 
 
  Judah--Zebulun--Naphtali; tribes by which they had been principally delivered, here put to represent the whole nation.

entries.title: Psalms 68:29
segments: The hearts of kings and rulers are in the hands of the Lord; and when he inclines them, they favor his people and become nursing fathers and mothers to his church.

entries.title: Psalms 68:30
segments: The multitude of the bulls, with the calves; the great, strong, and powerful; young and old.

entries.title: Psalms 68:31
segments:
Egypt; Ethiopia; representatives of the heathen world, especially Africa. 
 
The dark and polluted places of the earth, which are now full of the habitations of wickedness and cruelty, shall one day all be enlightened and purified, and become a habitation for God through his Spirit.

entries.title: Psalms 68:33
segments: Heavens of heavens; the highest heavens.

entries.title: Psalms 68:35
segments: Out of thy holy places; literally, out of thy sanctuaries.  The plural is used here, and in
, (in the Hebrew,) and

, in reference to the various divisions of the sanctuary. 
 
The God of salvation to his people will be the God of vengeance to those who continue to rebel against him.  He is a light and glory to those who serve him, but to his persevering enemies a consuming fire.
